transcript:
User: Hello? Yeah... I got your card. You help with phones, right?
Agent: Yeah, that’s us — we help make sure you don’t lose business when the phone rings and no one can grab it.  

Got it, so you got our card… was that from Jay stopping by in person, or did you find it somewhere else?
User: Uh, Jay stopped by, I think. Left it on my porch.
Agent: Gotcha, so he dropped it off in person.  

When you saw “we help with phones,” what were you hoping it could fix for you?
User: Uh, sometimes I miss calls when I'm busy. Maybe, uh, make sure I don't miss too many?
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — you’re busy actually doing the work, not just sitting by the phone.  

So when a call comes in and you’re tied up, what usually happens — does it go to voicemail, ring out, or sometimes just get ignored until later?
User: Uh, it usually goes to voicemail, I think. Maybe ten, fifteen calls? Not too sure.
Agent: Got it, so they’re mostly hitting voicemail and we’re talking maybe 10–15 calls.  

When they land in voicemail, do people usually leave a message and wait, or do you feel like some of those just hang up and call the next guy?
User: Uh, some leave messages, but I think some hang up. Not everyone waits around.
Agent: Yeah, that’s what we hear a lot — the ones who hang up are usually the ones turning into money for somebody else.  

So on your end, what kind of work do you do — what industry are you in?
User: Uh, I run a small landscaping business. Just, you know, yards and gardens, stuff like that.
Agent: Nice, got it — small landscaping, yards and gardens.  

When those 10–15 calls a week hit voicemail and some hang up, do you feel like you’re actually losing jobs from that, or has it not really hit you in the wallet yet?
User: Uh, maybe losing a few jobs, not sure. Hard to tell if it's really affecting the wallet.
Agent: Yeah, totally get that — it’s tricky because you can’t see the jobs you never booked.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through the math on what those missed calls might be costing you each month?
User: Uh, no, I don't think anyone's done that. Never really thought about the math like that.
Agent: Makes sense, most folks haven’t — you’re busy actually doing the work, not running spreadsheets.  

Mind if we do a super quick back-of-the-napkin calc together, just to see if it’s a real leak or not?
User: Uh, yeah, I guess that's fine. Quick's good. Not too sure about the numbers though.
Agent: Totally fine, we’ll just ballpark it together.  

So roughly for you, how many calls a week do you think actually hit voicemail instead of a real person — would you say closer to 5, 10, or more like 15?
User: Uh, maybe closer to 10 or 15? Hard to say exactly.
Agent: Got it, let’s split the difference and call it about 12 a week.  

Of those 12 that hit voicemail, how many do you think would actually turn into jobs if you caught them live — maybe half, more, or less?
User: Uh, no idea, but maybe half? Could be more, just not sure.
Agent: Yeah, that’s fair, let’s call it about half to keep it simple.  

And when you do land a job from one of these calls, what’s a typical ticket for you — like an average job, are we talking a couple hundred bucks, closer to $500, or more?
Agent: Perfect, let’s use 400 as a working number.  

So with what you gave me, that’s roughly $2,400 a week — about $10,300 a month — in work that could be slipping away just from calls you can’t grab; does that feel about right when you hear it out loud?
User: Uh, depends on the job. Maybe four hundred? Or five hundred? Not really sure.
Agent: Yeah, totally, it’ll swing a bit job to job — using that 400 number we walked through, though, that still puts you in that ballpark of losing a few grand a week just because you’re on a mower instead of on the phone.  

If there was a way to have every one of those calls answered, questions handled, and jobs booked for you while you’re out working — without hiring another person — is that something you’d actually want to fix, or more of a “nice to have”?
User: Uh, sounds good, I guess. Would be helpful if it works without hiring more people.
Agent: Makes sense — that’s exactly the gap we fill: we answer the calls you miss, book the work, and you don’t add payroll.  

So, to actually see how this would look with your numbers, let’s do a quick 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay this week — what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Uh, maybe tomorrow? Need some time to think. I'm a bit slow with these things.
Agent: Totally get that — no rush on decisions, this is just to see it clearly.  

Real quick — if I could guarantee you 5 to 10 extra jobs a month, would that be worth 20 minutes of your time?
User: Uh, yeah, sounds good. If it helps with extra jobs, maybe worth a try.
Agent: Nice, that’s exactly what this is for — see if it actually turns into extra jobs for you.  

First thing, what’s your first name?
User: Uh, it's Pedro. Just trying to see if it helps with all those missed calls and things, you know?
Agent: Got it, Pedro, and yeah — this is exactly for those missed calls.  

And your last name, so I pull up the right Pedro when we set this up?
User: Uh, last name's Martinez. Hope this helps with the calls and such.
Agent: Perfect, Pedro Martinez, got you.  

And what’s the name of your landscaping company?
User: Uh, just called Pedro's Landscaping. Nothing too fancy, just me and some tools.
Agent: Nice, Pedro's Landscaping — keeps it simple.  

Quick one: is the number you’re calling from right now the best one to text you a confirmation for that walkthrough?
User: Uh, yeah, this number's fine. Texts are okay. Make sure I get all the info, though.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use this number for the text.  

Quick check — you’re on Central time, right?
User: Uh, no, I'm on Eastern time. Just make sure the time's right for any messages or calls.
Agent: Gotcha, Eastern time, thanks for clearing that up.  

So for the 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay, I can get you in as soon as Wednesday at 4:00 PM or Thursday at 11:45 AM your time — which one feels easier for you?
User: Uh, Thursday at 11:45 AM sounds good. Need a bit more time to get ready.
Agent: Perfect, Thursday at 11:45 AM Eastern with Jay it is.  

Just to be sure we can text you the confirmation and link, what’s the cell number you want that sent to?
User: Uh, send it to my cell, it's 555-123-4567. I'll keep an eye out for it.
Agent: Got it, we’ll use 555-123-4567 for the confirmation text.  

So just to confirm — you’re all set for this Thursday at 11:45 AM Eastern with Jay for the 20‑minute walkthrough, no commitment, just to see if it can actually save those missed‑call jobs, right?
User: Uh, yeah, Thursday at 11:45 AM with Jay. No commitment, just to see if it helps.
Agent: Perfect, Pedro — I’ve got you locked in for Thursday at 11:45 AM Eastern with Jay for that 20‑minute walkthrough, no commitment, just to see if it actually saves those missed‑call jobs. You’ll get a text at 555-123-4567 with the details; just keep an eye on it and reply if anything changes, and Jay will call you at that time. Thanks for taking the time today and have a great rest of your day!
